description: On 1 October 2025, a Zamfara militia abducted six people, including two LGA councillors and an Imam in the Tsauni community, on the outskirts of Gusau (Gusau, Zamfara). The militia later released three individuals, killed the Imam, and took the two councillors with them. There was 1 fatality.

On 1 October 2025, at night, an unidentified armed group attacked Bethel Farm in Ejiba (Yagba West, Kogi). A KSVS member confronted the attackers while trying to repel the assault, but they burned his motorcycle. They also abducted 3 individuals from the town. Earlier in the morning, the attackers shot and killed 1 person along the Ejiba and Odo-Eri road (coded separately). There were no casualties.

On 1 October 2025, in the morning, an unidentified armed group shot and killed 1 bread merchant between Ejiba and Odo-Eri, location coded to the closest populated area, Odo Eri (Yagba West, Kogi). The attackers then attacked Ejiba at night and abducted 3 people after a firefight with a KSVS member (coded separately).

On 1 October 2025, an unidentified armed group sporadically fired shots to scare residents and abducted two brothers from their cassava farm in the Bokungi Zambufu community, also called Bokugi (Edu, Kwara).

On 1 October 2025, a Niger militia attacked Ibeto (Magama, Niger), killing 4 people, injuring 11, and abducting nine others. They moved from house to house, grabbing people and looting livestock. The militia attacked the village the day before and continued their assault into the next day (coded separately). 4 fatalities split across 2 events. 2 fatalities were coded to this event. The militia demanded 150 million naira before releasing 17 of the 30 captives after holding them for 54 days.

On 1 October 2025, a Niger militia abducted a human rights lawyer and about 12 other residents, including his daughter and two aids in the Gbaja community, location coded to the LGA HQ, Kagara (Rafi, Niger). The lawyer had previously shared information about the militia's movement on Facebook, showing their movement to Ibeto. The armed group fired into the air, looted homes, and took the victims into a nearby forest.

On 1 October 2025, an unidentified armed group abducted seven commuters along the Itobe-Anyagba road, near the Ojuwo Olijo forest, location coded to the midpoint between the two places, Ochadam (Ofu, Kogi). Eight passengers were on the bus, but one managed to escape during the interception.

On 1 October 2025, troops of the 222 Battalion and CJTF conducted clearance operations in the villages of Mittiri, Loskuri, Tamsu Ngamdu, and Wonori, locations coded to one of the villages, Tamsu Ngamdua (Mafa, Borno). The soldiers killed 1 ISWAP/Boko Haram (JAS) member and rescued some hostages. They also recovered one motorcycle.

On 1 October 2025, an unidentified armed group abducted a veterinary doctor and his three children in Kungabokun near Byazhin (Bwari, FCT). They killed the doctor (his body was found but the date of the killing was unspecified) and held his children hostage. There was 1 fatality.

On 1 October 2025, a Katsina militia (described as bandits) attacked the Dugun Muazu village (Sabuwa, Katsina), killing 1 farmer and abducting four others. The attack occurred in the context of a peace agreement between the militia groups and the residents.

On 1 October 2025, a Zamfara militia opened fire on miners, killing 1 at the Kokambam mining site in Magami district (Gusau, Zamfara). The incident nearly sparked an ethnic conflict, but the police managed to calm the situation.
On 1 October 2025, a Sokoto militia abducted three people in Sabon Gari Liman (Wurno, Sokoto) and looted an unspecified number of livestock.

On 1 October 2025, Boko Haram (JAS) killed 8 people, including 3 police officers, 3 CJTF members, and 2 farmers, in the village of Kawuri, coded to the LGA HQ Bama (Bama, Borno). The militants also looted a police van.

On 1 October 2025, Nigerian troops repelled an attempted incursion by a Zamfara militia (described as bandits) into the Tsunami, Bulunku, and Mareri communities, coded to the LGA HQ, Gusau (Gusau, Zamfara). Casualties unknown.

On 1 October 2025, a Zamfara militia (described as bandits) injured two VSN: Vigilante Society of Nigeria (described as VGN) members and abducted at least ten civilians in Saminaka, coded to the LGA HQ, Gusau (Gusau, Zamfara)
On 1 October 2025, a Zamfara militia (described as bandits) killed 1 man and injured three others in Yanwari, also spelled Yanware (Tsafe, Zamfara).

On 2 October 2025, an unidentified armed group opened fire sporadically and abducted 1 police officer (likely off-duty as he was returning from a work assignment after his colleagues had fled along the Patigi-Lade road, location coded to the midpoint Gbog (Pategi, Kwara). The police officers were returning from their official duty at Pategi when they were ambushed. There were no casualties.

On 2 October 2025, an unidentified armed group abducted 7 people along Wukari-Zaki Biam Road at Kasuwan Shanu, location coded to the closest populated area, Wukari (Wukari, Taraba). The abductors abandoned five hostages when security forces pursued them.

On 2 October 2025, a Sokoto militia attacked the Kaurare community in Alkamu ward (Wurno, Sokoto), killing and injuring an unspecified number of people. They also abducted some residents. They abducted some women in Sabon Birni LGA (coded separately). Unspecified number of fatalities coded as 3.

Around 2 October 2025 (between 2 - 3 October), a Sokoto militia (described as bandits) abducted at least ten women gathering firewood in Sabon Birni LGA, location coded to LGA HQ, Sabon Birni (Sabon Birni, Sokoto).
On 2 October 2025, a Niger militia attacked Tungar Gari village, location coded to the LGA HQ, Kontagora (Kontagora, Niger), killing 1 person and abducting several others, including women.

On 2 October 2025, a Kaduna militia attacked a commercial vehicle along Awon-Kachia road, location coded to the midpoint between the two places, Ankuwa (Kachia, Kaduna). The militia shot and killed 2 people, including the driver and a youth. They abducted some passengers, while others managed to escape.
On 2 October 2025, unidentified armed individuals kidnapped a herder in Jinkasa, coded to Azu (Tafa, Niger), a close populated place in the area.

On 2 October 2025, unidentified armed individuals clashed with the Nigerian police in Igoba (Akure North, Ondo). The attackers stormed the royal palace, attempted to kill the royal leader, injured a woman (she was taken to a hospital), and took her belongings. The police arrested ten suspects. There were no fatalities.

Around 2 October 2025 (as reported), an unidentified armed group killed an abducted evangelical pastor in the area of Ekati (Pategi, Kwara), as the ransom was not paid fully. The pastor had been previously abducted in late August by an unidentified armed group in the same area (coded separately).
On 2 October 2025, unidentified armed individuals killed 2 civilians travelling through Rafin-Azum, near Garam (Tafa, Niger).

On 2 October 2025, Boko Haram (JAS) militants killed 5 people, including three hunters and two local vigilantes/self-defense militia (coded as Konduga communal militia) members (likely armed), in attacks on Subdiburayee, coded to the closest populated area Dalwa (Konduga, Borno), and on Dalwa (coded separately). The militants also looted five bags of maize in both localities and warned members of the district heads' committees that there would be reprisals if they reported the attacks to the army. 5 fatalities split across 2 events. 2 fatalities were coded to this event.

On 2 October 2025, Boko Haram (JAS) killed 5 people, including three hunters and two local vigilantes/self-defense militia (coded as Konduga communal militia) members (likely armed), in attacks on Dalwa (Konduga, Borno) and Subdiburayee (coded separately). The militants also looted five bags of maize and warned members of the district heads' committees that there would be reprisals if they reported the attacks to the army. 5 fatalities split across 2 events. 3 fatalities were coded to this event.

On 2 October 2025, a Sokoto militia clashed with police and local vigilantes/self-defense militia (coded as Binji communal militia) in the village of Dalijan, coded to the LGA HQ Binji (Binji, Sokoto), after the militants abducted the wife of the local Miyatti Allah chairman. The woman was rescued, and one militant was arrested. There were no fatalities.
On 2 October 2025, ISSP (locally known as Lakurawa) killed 1 person in the village of Baliyo, coded to the ward HQ Bunkari (Binji, Sokoto).
On 2 October 2025, a Sokoto militia killed 2 persons and injured one in attacks on the villages of Maribi and Bagudu, coded to the LGA HQ Isa (Isa, Sokoto). The militants also abducted nine persons.

Around 2 October 2025 (as reported), an unidentified armed group abducted six individuals in an unspecified location in Katsina Ala LGA, coded to the LGA HQ Katsina-Ala (Katsina Ala, Benue). Nigerian military forces rescued the six victims on 2 October. No further details available.
On 2 October 2025, a Sokoto militia (described as bandits) injured one man and abducted seven farmers in the outskirts of Isa also spelled Isah (Isa, Sokoto).
On 2 October 2025, a Sokoto militia (described as bandits) injured three persons during an attack on Take, coded to the LGA HQ, Sobon Birni (Sabon Birni, Sokoto).
On 3 October 2025, Nigerian troops clashed with a Katsina militia, killing 3 along the Zango way, location coded to the nearest populated area, Zango (Kankara, Katsina).
Around 3 October 2025 (as reported), a Kaduna militia killed 1 person held hostage from the Ankwa area (Kachia, Kaduna). They killed him after collecting a ransom for his release.

On 3 October 2025, an unidentified armed group attacked and injured 1 man, who later managed to escape from the attackers in the Bareke area of Egbe (Yagba West, Kogi). The assailants then abducted his wife and two children and demanded a 100 million naira ransom for their release. There were no fatalities.
Around 3 October 2025 (as reported), the Nigerina troops clashed with ISWAP/Boko haram (JAS) in Kolori Karumi (Konduga, Borno) and Madagali LGA (coded separately). Casualties unknown.

Around 3 October 2025 (as reported), the Nigerina troops clashed with ISWAP/Boko haram (JAS) in Madagali LGA, location coded to LGHA HQ, Madagali (Madagali, Adamawa). The troops also clashed with the militia members in Kolori Karumi (coded separately). Casualties unknown.

Around 3 October 2025 (as reported), the Nigerian troops clashed with a Zamfara militia while repelling their attacks in Maradun LGA, location coded to the LGA HQ, Maradun (Maradun, Zamfara). They also clashed in Tsafe and Anka LGAs (coded separately). Casualties unknown.

Around 3 October 2025 (as reported), the Nigerian troops clashed with a Zamfara militia while repelling their attacks in Tsafe LGA, location coded to the LGA HQ, Tsafe (Tsafe, Zamfara). They also clashed in Maradun and Anka LGAs (coded separately). Casualties unknown.

Around 3 October 2025 (as reported), the Nigerian troops clashed with a Zamfara militia while repelling their attacks in Anka LGA, location coded to the LGA HQ, Anka (Anka, Zamfara). They also clashed in Maradun and Tsafe LGAs (coded separately). Casualties unknown.
Around 3 October 2025 (as reported), the Nigerian troops clashed with a Benue militia, killing 1 in Katsina Ala, LGA, location coded to the LGA HQ, Katsina-Ala (Katsina Ala, Benue).

On 3 October 2025, police and VSN clashed with ISSP fighters (locally known as Lakurawa) in Gorun Yamma village (Dandi Kamba, Kebbi). The security forces killed 3 ISSP members and injured an unspecified number of others who managed to escape with gunshot wounds. They recovered an unregistered vehicle and weapons.

On 3 October 2025, an unidentified armed group abducted a local trader and his two daughters, including a university student in the 200-level, in the Zhibi community near Dei-Dei (Abuja Municipal, FCT). Mobile phones were looted.
On 3 October 2025, Nigerian troops clashed with Boko Haram militants in Dipchari (Bama, Borno), killing 5 of them.

On 3 October 2025, overnight, suspected Boko Haram militants simultaneously attacked the Banki Divisional Police Headquarters, Immigration and Customs Service in Banki (Bama, Borno), as well as the Cameroonian Military camp in Amchide (coded separately). The attack was repelled. One police officer was injured during the clashes. There were no fatalities.

On 3 October 2025, an unidentified armed group clashed with a vigilante group and killed the local vigilantes/self-defense militia (coded as Magama communal militia) leader, in the area of Auna (Magama, Niger).

On 3 October 2025, overnight, a Katsina militia attacked the village of Ruwan Gora, coded to Ungwan Doro (Dandume, Katsina), a midpoint in the area. The attack resulted in the death and injury of villagers as well as the abduction of others. Unspecified fatalities coded as 3.

On 3 October 2025, overnight, an unidentified armed group attacked with machetes the Fulani settlement near Osara Dam, coded to Osara (Adavi, Kogi), a nearby location. The attack caused the death of 2 Fulani civilians and the injury of another one.
On 3 October 2025, an unidentified armed group kidnapped 7 civilians in the village of Dukku (Rijau, Niger).
On 3 October 2025, armed Fulani pastoralists attacked farmers in the area of Naka (Gwer West, Benue), killing 2 of them.

On 3 October 2025, armed Fulani pastoralists killed 1 farmer in Onoli (Agwu, Enugu), along the Enugu-Port Harcourt Highway, close to the border between Enugu and Abia states. This happened in a context of several attacks from pastoralists against farmers that caused residents of villages in the area out of their farmlands.

On 3 October 2025, suspected cult militia killed 1 man and injured his girlfriend in the Iyara area of Warri (Warri South, Delta). The victim was a carpenter and was shot in retaliation for his involvement in the stabbing and killing of a man who owed him money.
On 3 October 2025, a Sokoto militia abducted a woman in the village of Kube, coded to the LGA HQ Sabon Birni (Sabon Birni, Sokoto).
On 3 October 2025, a Sokoto militia abducted two persons who were heading to a farm in Pole, coded to the LGA HQ Sabon Birni (Sabon Birni, Sokoto).

On 3 October 2025, Boko Haram (JAS) killed 15 people, including two soldiers and 13 CJTF members and hunters, in an attack on the military base in Izge, also called Izge-Unore (Gwoza, Borno). The militants also set fire to an army truck and three pickup vehicles, and looted shops.

On 3 October 2025, Boko Haram (JAS) and Nigerian troops clashed at the military FOB in Benishek, coded to the LGA HQ Khaddamari (Jere, Borno). The army killed 10 militants and recovered seven motorcycles, seven AK-47 rifles, and ammunition.
On 3 October 2025, a Zamfara militia killed 2 persons, injured three, and abducted ten in Kwaren Ganuwa, also spelled Koran Ganawa (Tsafe, Zamfara).

On 3 October 2025, a Zamfara militia killed 3 persons and abducted an unspecified number in an unspecified location along the Mayanchi-Anka road in the Anka LGA, coded to Maikwonaga (Anka, Zamfara), a midpoint between the two locations.
On 3 October 2025, a Sokoto militia killed 1 person in the village of Dan Gulbi, coded to the LGA HQ Isa (Isa, Sokoto).

On 3 October 2025, a Sokoto militia (described as bandits) killed 2 people, injured 2 others, and abducted 15 others in the community of Kaurare, coded to the ward HQ, Alkamu (Wurno, Sokoto). The militants also looted livestock.

On 3 October 2025, ISSP (locally known as Lakurawa) injured an unspecified number of persons in the village of Labau, coded to the LGA HQ Binji (Binji, Sokoto). They also looted six heads of livestock.

On 3 October 2025, a Niger militia abducted 2 family members, a father and daughter, after abducting them from the Zhidu community, coded to the closest populated area, Garam (Tafa, Niger). The abductors received 12 million naira (approximately 8500 USD) ransom in tranches. They killed the daughter for being 'stubborn' around January 2026 (coded separately). They later declared that the father had died from a sickness.
On 3 October 2025, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists killed 1 man and injured an unspecified number of people in the village of Gako, coded to the ward HQ Rim (Riyom, Plateau).

On 3 October 2025, a Katsina militia (described as bandits) abducted two men and rustled a large number of cattle during an invasion in the Jere community in Kankia LGA, coded to LGA HQ, Kankia (Kankia, Katsina). The victims' whereabouts are unknown.
On 3 October 2025, a Sokoto militia (described as bandits) killed 2 Nigerian troops and injured two others in Sabon Gari Liman (Wurno, Sokoto) as the troops attempted to repel them for the community.

On 3 October 2025, a Zamfara militia (described as bandits) attacked and looted one rifle from members of the Zamfara State Community Protection Guards in the vicinity of the Federal Government College, Anka (Anka, Zamfara). Casualties unknown.

On 4 October 2025, a hunter shot and killed 1 civilian during a stop-and-search operation near Mafa LGA, location coded to LGA HQ, Mafa (Mafa, Borno). The hunter was a reformed Boko Haram (JAS) member involved in a counterterrorism effort. He fired and killed the victim when the latter refused to pay 1,000 naira at a checkpoint.

On 4 October 2025, ISWAP ambushed a patrol of the Nigerian army along the Gwoza-Bitta road, coded to Lokodisa Adamu (Gwoza, Borno), a midpoint between the two locations. ISWAP claimed to have killed 4 Nigerian soldiers, injured 3 others, as well as seized several weapons, ammunition, a motorcycle, and burned some of the assets. Other sources confirmed ISWAP claims.

On 4 October 2025, the CJTF clashed with a Katsina militia (described as bandits) on the Kankara - Yan Tumaki road, coded to Tudu (Kankara, Katsina). The CJTF 'neutralized' and killed an unspecified six militia members, recovered three motorcycles and returned them to their owners. Unspecified fatalities coded as 3.

Around 4 October 2025 (as reported), the Nigerian police, supported by vigilantes (coded as Gorun Yamma Communal Militia), repelled the attack and clashed with ISSP members (locally known as Lakurawa), killing 3 militants, in Gorun Yamma (Dandi Kamba, Kebbi). Many other militants were injured.

On 4 October 2025, rival unidentified cult militias clashed in the Onireke and Isashi areas within Badagry (Lagos Island, Lagos), leading to the injury of three civilians, of whom 1 died in hospital. The police intervened by arresting five suspects and recovered one pistol, two shotguns, ammunition and other weapons.
On 4 October 2025, a Zamfara militia killed 2 persons and abducted three in Maru (Maru, Zamfara).
On 4 October 2025, overnight, a Zamfara militia attacked Kamani, coded to Talata Mafara (Talata Mafara, Zamfara), the LGA capital. Casualties unknown.
On 4 October 2025, overnight, an unidentified armed group attacked multiple villages in the area of Pangu Gari (Rafi, Niger), near the Gwabtai river. Casualties unknown.

Around 4 October 2025 (as reported), unidentified armed individuals killed 1 civilian in Abuja (Abuja Municipal, Federal Capital Territory). The attack shortly followed the kidnapping of the civilian and his three children.
On 4 October 2025, overnight, an unidentified armed group attacked villages in Yagba West, coded to Odo Ere (Yagba West, Kogi), the LGA capital, killing 27 civilians.
On 4 October 2025, a Katsina militia abducted a member of the Community Watch Corps from his residence in Dantankari (Dandume, Katsina).
On 4 October 2025, Boko Haram (JAS) killed 44 people, including four soldiers, in Kumshe (Bama, Borno). The militants also set fire to four pickup trucks.
On 4 October 2025, farmers and a Fulani pastoralists clashed in Ngurno (Monguno, Borno) over a grazing land dispute. 1 farmer was killed.

On 4 October 2025, a Katsina militia and the CJTF clashed at an unspecified location in Dan-Musa LGA along the road between Kankara and Yantumaki, coded to Danali (Dan-Musa, Katsina), a midpoint between both towns. The clash broke out after the militia had blocked the road to rob travelers. 3 militiamen were killed and three stolen motorcycles were recovered.

On 4 October 2025, Nigerian troops killed 7 persons, including six members of a Sokoto militia and one member of a community guard, during an operation at a militia hideout in the forest of Tidibale (Isa, Sokoto). The troops freed 66 abducted persons.
On 4 October 2025, a Zamfara militia killed 2 persons and abducted an unspecified number in Maru Town in the Talata Mafara LGA, coded to the LGA HQ Talata Mafara (Talata Mafara, Zamfara).
On 4 October 2025, a Zamfara militia killed 1 person after blocking a road leading to Kaura Namoda (Kaura Namoda, Zamfara).
On 4 October 2025, a Sokoto militia attacked (means unspecified) farmers in Gidan-Buwai (Rabah, Sokoto). There were no fatalities.
On 4 October 2025, a Sokoto militia attacked (means unspecified) farmers in Kundus (Rabah, Sokoto). There were no fatalities.
On 4 October 2025, a Sokoto militia attacked (means unspecified) farmers in Rarah (Rabah, Sokoto). There were no fatalities.
On 4 October 2025, a Sokoto militia attacked (means unspecified) farmers in Dudu-Barade (Rabah, Sokoto). There were no fatalities.
On 4 October 2025, niger militias (described as bandits) clashed amongst themselves in Dekala (Borgu, Niger). 9 bandits were killed and many others injured.

On 5 October 2025, Nigerian military, police, and ZCPG members engaged a Zamfara militia (described as bandits) in a firefight while responding to the militia's invasion of the Fakon Idi area in Jangebe District (Talata Mafara, Zamfara). The militia had killed 1 ZCPG member and injured two to three others for resisting abduction, and abducted fifteen others before the troops arrived. They fled into the bush when security agencies engaged them. There was 1 fatality.

On 5 October 2025, a Zamfara militia (described as bandits) attacked a farm in Kwaren Ganuwa village, also spelled Koran Ganawa (Tsafe, Zamfara), killing 3 farmers and abducting at least ten others. The victims were working under duress on a farm owned by another militia before a different group invaded the farm and took them away.

On 5 October 2025, a Zamfara militia (described as bandits) shot and killed between 1 and 3 men, including a newlywed man who was shot for resisting abduction, and abducted his bride among at least fifteen others in Maru (Maru, Zamfara).
On 5 October 2025, overnight, ISWAP assaulted the Forward Operating Base of the Nigerian military in Rann (Kala Balge, Borno). The attack was repelled, and at least 2 militants were killed.

On 5 October 2025, the Nigerian army clashed with an unidentified armed group between Tornyi and Tarhembe (Takum, Taraba), during a clearance operation against suspected bases of unidentified armed groups in the area. The unidentified armed group retreated in the bush. There were no fatalities. The army recovered one AK-47, one motorcycle and ammunition.

On 5 October 2025, suspected Boko Haram militants clashed with a mixed contingent composed of Nigerian Military, Police forces, CJTF, and hunters in Malari (Guzamala, Borno). The clash followed Boko Haram attack against the village and the kidnapping of three residents. The mixed contingent repelled the attack. Casualties unknown.

On 5 October 2025, armed militants clashed with local vigilantes in Rani Ramat (Pategi, Kwara). Vigilantes intervened in response to the attack by armed militants against villagers praying at the mosque and the abduction of the village chief (coded separately). The clash resulted in the death of 1 vigilante and 1 militant. Several residents sought refuge in nearby villages. 2 fatalities coded.

On 5 October 2025, a Katsina militia (described as bandits) attacked Muslim worshippers during prayers in Gazari (Sabuwa, Katsina), killing 1 civilian and abducting several others. 11 people were confirmed missing.

On 5 October 2025, a Katsina militia attacked civilians on the road segment between Dayi and Tuge, coded to Tugen Na'alma (Malumfashi, Katsina). The militia killed 1 traveler, abducted several others, and looted motorcycles.
On 5 October 2025, an unidentified armed individual attacked civilians in front of military barracks in Ojo (Ojo, Lagos), killing 4 and injuring many others.
On 5 October 2025, armed Fulani pastoralists killed 1 civilian in the area of Tanda (Jema'a, Kaduna). There were no further details.

On 5 October 2025, Boko Haram (JAS) militants and Nigerian troops clashed at the military FOB in Mafa (Mafa, Borno) after the militants stormed the facility following an attack on the locality in which they killed 13 people (coded separately). The militants eventually withdrew. Casualties unknown.

On 5 October 2025, ISWAP militants and Nigerian troops clashed at a pumping station on the road between Gamboru Ngala and Kala Balge located within Ngala LGA, coded to Ngala (Ngala, Borno). Nigerian troops killed 1 ISWAP militant, and the group withdrew.

On 5 October 2025, Boko Haram (JAS) militants killed 13 people, including 10 farmers and three hunters, in an attack in Mafa (Mafa, Borno). The militants then clashed with Nigerian troops at the military FOB near the locality (coded separately).
On 5 October 2025, a Katsina militia killed 6 people and injured three in the community of Yar Tsakuwa, coded to the LGA HQ Malumfashi (Malumfashi, Katsina). The militia also abducted one person.
On 5 October 2025, a Zamfara militia (described as bandits) abducted seven women in Kamani, coded to its ward, Tashar Kuturu (Talata Mafara, Zamfara).

On 5 October 2025, CJTF: Civilian Joint Task Force members attacked a suspected Zamfara militia (described as bandits) in the Kwammaka Forest, coded to its ward, Birnin Magaji (Gummi, Zamfara). An unspecified number of militia members were killed, weapons and motorcycles were recovered, and an unspecified number of hostages were freed. Unspecified fatalities coded as 3.

On 6 October 2025, police and KSVS clashed with an unidentified armed group abducting passengers along the Okene-Auchi highway, location coded to the last town in Kogi State on the route, Okeni (Okene, Kogi). After receiving a distress call, the police swiftly intervened and engaged the captors, who had shot and injured 1 female passenger and abducted the remaining 10 people on board. Police rescued eight hostages after the clash, while the abductors managed to escape with two others. There were no fatalities.

On 6 October 2025, a suspected Berom militia shot and killed a 13-year-old Fulani pastoralist along with his 36 cows at Ndinn village in Fan district, also spelled Nding (Barkin Ladi, Plateau). About 49 other cows scattered and could not be accounted for. There was 1 fatality.

On 6 October 2025, a Katsina militia (described as bandits) attacked Kankia town (Kankia, Katsina), shooting people. They also abducted 2 women from the Bakin Kasuwa area of the town. Casualties unknown.

On 6 October 2025, the Aye (Black Axe) attacked and killed 3 members of Eiye in the Kajola area of Atan-Ota, also called Atan (Ado-Odo, Ogun). The killing was suspected to be reprisal for the killing of an Aye member by the Eiye a few weeks earlier (coded separately). The Aye members fired sporadically to scare people away before shooting at the three Eiye members.

On 6 October 2025, the Eiye killed 1 NBM member (Neo-Black Movement, an alternative name for Aye or Black Axe) in front of his house in the ECOWAS area of Ojo (Ojo, Lagos) for unknown reasons. The victim was also a community security personnel.
On 6 October 2025, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists attacked an unspecified village in the Fan district of Barkin Ladi LGA, coded to LGA HQ Barkin Ladi (Barkin Ladi).
On 6 October 2025, a member of Aye (Black Axe) stabbed and killed 1 person in the Ibusa area (Oshimili North, Delta) for unknown reasons. The attacker was arrested.

On 6 October 2025, an unidentified armed group opened fire on the vehicle of the Commander of the Osun Amotekun Corps along Ikirun Road, near Kobo, location coded to the closest populated area, Ikirun (Ifelodun, Osun). Bullets hit him, injuring him, and damaged his vehicle. There were no fatalities.

Around 6 October 2025 (as reported), the United Hunters Association clashed with a Kaduna militia in Yakawada (Giwa, Kaduna). The clashes resulted in the 'neutralization' (meaning killing) of 3 militia members, the death of the leader of the United Hunters Association in Giwa LGA, the injury of other hunters and the liberation of three abductees. 4 Fatalities coded.
On 6 October 2025, a Zamfara militia (described as bandits) attacked farmers and abducted at least fifteen of them on the outskirts of Shinkafi (Shinkafi, Zamfara). Casualties unknown.
On 6 October 2025, Boko Haram militants attacked Kirawa (Gwoza, Borno), killing 2 civilians and setting ablaze the palace of the district head and fifty other houses and shops.

On 6 October 2025, an unidentified armed group abducted the wife of an officer from the Nigerian Immigration Service along the Badagry-Mile Two expressway, location code to Mile Two (Amowo-Odofin, Lagos). The abductors initially demanded a 7 million naira ransom for her release, but later lowered it to 3 million naira.
On 6 October 2025, a Katsina militia abducted one person in Kankara (Kankara, Katsina).

On 6 October 2025, Boko Haram (JAS) militants killed 27 people, including seven police officers, in an attack on Limankara (Gwoza, Borno) that targeted mobile police barracks. The militants also looted three police SUVs and three AK-47 rifles.
On 6 October 2025, a Katsina militia killed 1 person and abducted another on the road between Musawa and Tuge, coded to Dan Janku (Musawa, Katsina), a midpoint between the two localities.
On 6 October 2025, a Katsina militia injured one person in an attack in Kakumi (Bakori, Katsina).
On 6 October 2025, two unidentified rival cult militias clashed in Makurdi-Wadata (Makurdi, Benue). 1 individual was killed.
On 6 October 2025, a Sokoto militia (described as bandits) killed 7 persons, including 2 men and 5 infants in Barazzaki, coded to the LGA HQ, Wurno (Wurno, Sokoto).
On 6 October 2025, a Zamfara militia (described as bandits) abducted two people near Kadaddaba village, coded to its ward, Ruwan Doruwa (Maru, Zamfara).
On 7 October 2025, a Zamfara militia opened fire sporadically to scare people and abducted 30 people from Zamfarawa village in Zugu district (Bukkuyum, Zamfara).

Many escaped with gunshot injuries while the troops recovered two AK-47 rifles, eight pump-action guns, four locally made pistols, three packets of cartridges (101 rounds), and four empty AK-47 magazines. Scores of fatalities coded as 20.

Around 30 January 2025 (week of), a Zamfara militia abducted 16 people, including the deputy Imam of a central mosque in Maru (Maru, Zamfara). The chief Imam was abducted about two weeks later (coded separately).
On 30 January 2025, a Zamfara militia attacked and killed 3 people and abducted nine others in Shinkafi town (Shinkafi, Zamfara). The hostages included four women.
On 30 January 2025, a Niger militia (described as bandits) clashed with Mahmuda on motorbikes in Bowya forest, Bowya, also spelled Boya (Borgu, Niger). 6 bandits and 5 Mahmuda were killed.

On 30 January 2025, a Niger militia (described as bandits) mounted an IVCP and attacked a passenger's vehicle on the Safeluna-Saabasi Road in Safeluna, also spelled Sanfeluna (Borgu, Niger). 3 civilians were killed and 2 were wounded. The militia was targeting a specific person but did not find him in the vehicle.
On 30 January 2025, ISWAP clashed with CJTF at a checkpoint in Warabe (Gwoza, Borno). 1 vigilante member was killed. ISWAP also looted a vehicle belonging to the CJTF members.

On 30 January 2025, CJTF members clashed with ISWAP militants in an ISWAP camp in Arri, also known as Arri Kurumiri (Konduga, Borno). The CJTF members retreated after several minutes. There were no casualties.
On 30 January 2025, Cameroonian military forces attacked a camp of an unidentified Ambazonian militia in Kpakya (Ussa, Taraba). Casualties unknown. No further details available.
On 30 January 2025, ISWAP militants abducted at least five travelers along a road in Azare, coded to the LGA HQ Buni Yadi (Gujba, Yobe).
On 30 January 2025, ISWAP killed 1 farmer and injured another in Warabe (Gwoza, Borno). There were no further details.

On 30 January 2025, local vigilantes (coded as Turare communal militia) deployed and clashed with a Katsina militia (described as bandits) in an unspecified settlement near Turare (Dutsinma, Katsina), after the militia had attacked the community. 1 militia member was killed, and another was injured.

On 30 January 2025, Nigerian troops supported by the KSCWC clashed with a Katsina militia (described as bandits) at an illegal checkpoint along the Turare road in Turare (Dutsinma, Katsina). 11 militia members were killed.

Around 31 January 2025 (as reported), a CJTF group tortured and killed 1 person in Laminga (Nasarawa, Nassarawa) over a theft allegation. They dumped his body in the village. Police later arrested the CJTF members.

On 31 January 2025, an unidentified armed group abducted the chairperson of the Abia State Independent Electoral Commission from his residence in Okigwe (Okigwe, Imo). He was abducted for an unknown reason while holding a meeting with some Abia State University lecturers.

On 31 January 2025, an unidentified cult group shot and killed 2 members of a rival cult group in Onne (Okrika, Rivers). The victims' members avenged their deaths and killed their assailant the following day, coded separately.

On 31 January 2025, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists attacked and killed 7 people in Lighitlubang village in Bungha district (Mangu, Plateau) for an unknown reason. The victims included two couples and a child. 2 more bodies were later found in the bush.

On 31 January 2025, an unidentified armed group shot and killed the Chief Security Officer of the Adokiye Amiesimaka Stadium and his son at their residence in Igwuruta-Ali, also called Igwuruta (Ikwerre, Rivers). The killing was suspected to be connected with his official responsibilities. There were 2 fatalities.

On 31 January 2025, an unidentified armed group from Ibasa (likely a cult militia due to the nature of the attack and their prevalence in the area) killed 2 people and injured many others in Ijegun Egba (Amowo-Odofin, Lagos) for unknown reasons. They carried the body of one of their victims back to their location in Ibasa.

On 31 January 2025, armed Fulani pastoralists clashed with armed Adorgo farmers in Adorgo village in Ugbaam ward (Ukum, Benue) and Tse-tor village in Gboko LGA, coded separately. The clash erupted over unknown reasons. There was 1 fatality split across 2 events. 0 fatality coded to this event.

On 31 January 2025, armed Fulani pastoralists clashed with armed Tse-tor farmers in Tse-tor village (Gboko, Benue) and Adorgo village in Ugbaam ward in Ukum LGA, coded separately. The clash erupted over unknown reasons. There was 1 fatality split across 2 events. 1 fatality coded to this event.

Around 31 January 2025 (as reported), a Zamfara militia abducted 12 people in Shanawa village (Shinkafi, Zamfara). They released the hostages on 28 January 2025 after receiving a 12 million naira ransom.

On 31 January 2025, ISWAP/Boko Haram (JAS) abducted one person after they missed their primarily targeted of an aid worker (INGO) at a guesthouse in Ngala town (Ngala, Borno). The hostage later escaped from the abductors.

On 31 January 2025, and over three days (all coded separately), armed Fulani pastoralists attacked Eha Amufu (Isi Uzo, Enugu). Over the three-day period, they killed an unspecified number of people. Unspecified number of fatalities coded as 3. 3 fatalities split across three events. 1 fatality coded to this event.
On 31 January 2025, ISWAP killed 1 elderly person in Goni Kurmi (Bama, Borno). They also burned houses and shops before retreating.
On 31 January 2025, a Katsina militia abducted an unspecified number of people from Runka (Safana, Katsina).
